name: Never write he/she or s/he

source.section: Inclusive language > Pronouns in generic references
source.quote: Never write he/she or s/he.

message: A slashed pronoun pair is hard to read aloud and still leaves people out.
fix: Rewrite to "you", to a plural, to "the" or "a", to a role name, or to singular "they".

flag: The admin decides whether he/she approves the request.
pass: Admins decide whether they approve the request.

name: Gendered pronoun for a generic person

source.section: Inclusive language > Pronouns in generic references
source.quote: Don't use he, him, his, she, her, or hers for a generic person.

message: A generic person, such as "the admin" or "a reviewer", gets no gendered pronoun. Gendered pronouns are right only for a named person who uses them and in direct quotations.
fix: In order of preference: rewrite to "you", rewrite to a plural, use "the" or "a", name the role, or use singular "they".

flag: A reviewer sees his own tasks on the home screen.
The admin can reset passwords if he or she has the right permissions.
pass: Reviewers see their own tasks on the home screen.

name: Gender-neutral words

source.quote: chair, moderator | chairman. staff, workforce | manpower. sales representative | salesman. staffed | manned. people, humanity | mankind. artificial, synthetic | man-made.

message: The guide's table gives a gender-neutral word for this one.
fix: Use the replacement from the table.

flag: The help desk is manned around the clock.
pass: The help desk is staffed around the clock.

name: Terms that carry bias

source.section: Inclusive language > Terms that carry bias
source.quote: primary, replica | master, slave. main (branch) | master (branch). blocklist, allowlist | blacklist, whitelist. legacy, exempt | grandfathered. quick check, confidence check | sanity check. placeholder, sample | dummy. stop responding | hang.

message: The guide replaces this term. A term that's part of a command, a setting, or an API stays as written, so flag that case for the product team instead of editing the prose.
fix: Use the replacement from the table.

flag: Add the domain to the whitelist.
Merge into the master branch.
Use dummy data in the sample.
If the app hangs, restart it.
pass: Add the domain to the allowlist.
Merge into the main branch.
Use placeholder data in the sample.

name: Combat and violence metaphors

source.section: Inclusive language > Combat and violence metaphors
source.quote: Don't borrow language from combat when you mean something ordinary. Also avoid strike and troops.

message: Combat language makes an ordinary action sound violent and translates badly. A technical term such as the `kill` command stays as written.
fix: Use the plain word from the guide's table.

flag: This update eliminates duplicate tasks.
Limit the blast radius of a bad deploy.
pass: This update removes duplicate tasks.
Limit the impact of a bad deploy.

name: Disability terms and metaphors

source.quote: Write uses a wheelchair, not wheelchair-bound. Don't use stricken with or suffering from. Don't use a disability as a metaphor.

message: Focus on people, not conditions, and don't borrow a disability as a metaphor.
fix: Use the plain replacement. "The outage crippled the service" becomes "The outage stopped the service."

flag: The outage crippled the service.
Teams blind to the risk lose data.
pass: The outage stopped the service.
Teams unaware of the risk lose data.

name: Don't use age as shorthand for skill

source.quote: "So easy your grandparents can use it" becomes "Easy to set up."

message: Age is not a measure of skill.
fix: Say what makes it easy: "Easy to set up."

flag: So easy your grandparents can use it.
pass: Easy to set up.

name: Avoid cultural appropriation

source.quote: Avoid slang and anything that could read as cultural appropriation, such as spirit animal or tribe for a team.

message: These words borrow from cultures that aren't the reader's or the writer's.
fix: Write "team", "group", or "meeting".

flag: Find your tribe in the community forum.
pass: Find your team in the community forum.

name: Avoid idioms and sports metaphors

source.quote: Avoid idioms and sports metaphors. "Out of the box" becomes "by default." "A ballpark figure" becomes "a rough estimate."

message: Idioms don't translate. Only the two the guide names are checked here. Add rows as you find more.
fix: Use the plain phrase from the guide.

flag: Sync works out of the box.
Heads up: your access key expires soon.
pass: Sync works by default.

name: Avoid unusual contractions

source.quote: Avoid unusual ones (it'd, should've, there're) and contractions of nouns.

message: Common contractions sound natural. Unusual ones slow readers down and trip translation tools.
fix: Spell it out.

flag: It'd be faster to filter first.
There're three options.
pass: It would be faster to filter first.
It's faster to filter first.

name: Use common contractions

source.quote: Common contractions such as it's, you're, don't, can't, and isn't make text sound like a person wrote it.

message: The guide's voice is a capable colleague, and colleagues use contractions. Legal text keeps its exact wording.
fix: Use the contraction unless the text is legal wording or the full form carries emphasis.

flag: The report does not include test accounts.
pass: The report doesn't include test accounts.
The report excludes test accounts.

name: US spelling

source.quote: US spelling (color, organize, center).

message: The guide uses US English spelling. If your team writes another variety, change this rule in your fork.
fix: Use the US spelling.

flag: Choose a colour for the label.
The sync was cancelled.
pass: Choose a color for the label.
The sync was canceled.

name: Its is possessive, it's means it is

source.quote: Its is possessive. It's means it is or it has.

message: This is the one homophone pair a pattern can catch safely. "It's own" needs no apostrophe, and "its a" needs one.
fix: Use "its" for possession and "it's" for "it is" or "it has".

flag: The team has it's own workspace.
Its a scheduled period when updates can run.
pass: The team has its own workspace.
It's a scheduled period when updates can run.

name: Don't write (s) for one or more

source.quote: Don't write (s) to mean one or more. "Select the file(s)" becomes "Select one or more files."

message: "(s)" asks the reader to parse two sentences at once and breaks screen readers.
fix: Write "one or more files", or use the plural.

flag: Select the file(s) to upload.
pass: Select one or more files to upload.

name: No apostrophe in acronym plurals or possessives

source.quote: Add a lowercase s to make an acronym plural, with no apostrophe: APIs, URLs. Don't make an acronym possessive. "The API's limits" becomes "the API limits".

message: An apostrophe makes an acronym plural look possessive, and the guide bans the possessive too. Decades take no apostrophe either.
fix: Write "APIs", "the API limits", or "the 2020s".

flag: Both API's return JSON.
Check the API's limits.
Designs from the 2010's.
pass: Both APIs return JSON.
Check the API limits.
Designs from the 2010s.

name: Don't write firstly

source.quote: Ordinals. Spell out first through ninth. Don't write firstly.

message: "First" already works as an adverb.
fix: Write "first", "second", "third".

flag: Firstly, open the project.
pass: First, open the project.

name: No please, sorry, oops, or unfortunately

source.quote: No please, sorry, oops, or unfortunately.

message: Politeness words add length and, in an error, sound like blame or panic. Say what happened and what to do.
fix: Delete the word and lead with the action.

flag: Oops! We couldn't save your file.
Please select a smaller file.
pass: The file didn't save because the disk is full. Free up space and try again.

name: Never "Are you sure?" or "Warning!" as a title

source.quote: The title is a question or a statement that names the object: "Delete this project?" Never "Are you sure?" or "Warning!"

message: A confirmation names the object and the consequence so the reader knows what they're deciding.
fix: Name the action and the object: "Delete this project? Its tasks move to your default project."

flag: Are you sure? [Yes] [No]
pass: Delete this project? Its tasks move to your default project.

name: "Something went wrong" is the last resort

source.quote: One message per known cause. "Something went wrong" is the last resort, not the default.

message: A generic error gives the reader nothing to act on. If the cause is known, name it and say what to do.
fix: Write one message per known cause: what happened, why if the reader can act on it, and what to do next.

flag: An unexpected error occurred.
pass: The connector lost its link to the sync API. Check network access to the endpoint.

name: Never "click here" as link text

source.quote: Link text names the destination or the result. Never "click here," and never "learn more" on its own.

message: "Here" tells the reader nothing about where the link goes, and screen readers list links by their text.
fix: Name the destination or the result: "View the sharing rules."

flag: Click here to view the sharing rules.
pass: View the sharing rules.

name: "Learn more" needs an object

source.quote: never "learn more" on its own.

message: On its own, "Learn more" doesn't say what the reader will learn.
fix: Add the subject: "Learn more about recommendations."

flag: Learn more
Select Learn more to continue.
pass: Learn more about recommendations

name: Don't point with above or below

source.quote: Don't point with "above" or "below." Link to the section by name.

message: Position breaks when the layout changes or a screen reader reads the page in order.
fix: Name the section and link to it, or name the control.

flag: Follow the steps described above.
Select the button on the left.
pass: Follow the steps in Invite people.
Select Save.

name: Alt text doesn't start with "Image of"

source.quote: Give every informative image alt text that says what it shows. Don't start with "Image of."

message: A screen reader already announces that this is an image.
fix: Describe what the image shows or does: "The Sharing tab with Invite people selected."

flag: ![Screenshot of the sharing dialog](img/share.png)
pass: ![The Sharing tab with Invite people selected](img/share.png)

name: Informative image with no alt text

source.quote: Give every informative image alt text that says what it shows. A decorative image gets empty alt text.

message: This image has no alt text. That's right for a decorative image and wrong for a screenshot or any image that carries information.
fix: Add alt text that says what the image shows, or leave it empty if the image is decorative.

flag: ![](img/share.png)
pass: ![The Sharing tab](img/share.png)
